question: Is the C(n,2) in QOU.Braiding.card_allPairs_le_length the same object as the C(A,2) in QOU.MassTheory.exchangeDet_pow_two_le_four?

verdict.summary: Not the same object. The shared C(n,2) is |E(K_n)| in both places, so the vocabulary is genuinely shared -- but that is what 'pairwise' MEANS, not evidence of common content. The bounds run in opposite directions on different quantities (lower bound on a word length vs upper bound on a log-det ratio), and no bridge exists because word length does not control any trace-derived magnitude.
verdict.trap_recorded: The tempting inference 'the braiding has no n-ary generator, so the extensive term cannot be super-pairwise' is a CATEGORY ERROR of the kind AGENTS.md names: a Markov trace of a word in 2-strand letters is already a many-body object. prop:pairwise-interaction-decomposition forbids a super-pairwise GENERATOR, not a super-pairwise VALUE. The saturation cap's conclusion stands untouched.

length_does_not_control_magnitude.point: Word length is not monotone in anything the binding reads. The Markov trace of a length-2 word here equals that of the empty word, so a LOWER bound on letters induces no lower bound on a trace-derived magnitude. The crossing bound therefore cannot constrain rho_A from below, which is the only direction that would interact with an UPPER cap.
